name: UniTel Voice
summary: Virtual business phone system for small teams. Get a toll-free or local number with auto-attendant, call routing and a mobile app — no hardware.
best_for: solopreneurs and small teams that want a professional toll-free or local number, auto-attendant and call routing on their existing phones — no hardware
skip_if: you need integrated video meetings, team chat and a full contact center, or you have no need for a separate business line at all
honest_knock: It's a virtual phone layer, not a full unified-comms suite — you won't find the deep team messaging, video meetings and contact-center features pricier platforms bundle. For a solo founder or small team that just needs a professional number, auto-attendant and call routing, that focus is exactly the point; for a larger org wanting one platform for everything, it will feel thin.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per month (1 user, unlimited minutes, one phone number)
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-24 on signup.unitelvoice.com/pick-plan, where unitelvoice.com/pricing now lands) Three plans, no contracts: Solo $9.99/mo, Team $19.99/mo and Office $29.99/mo, each with one toll-free or local number and unlimited calling and texting. Yearly billing is charged as $84, $168 and $252 a year (the cards say "Save $36/year", $72 and $108); the comparison table shows that as $6.99, $13.99 and $20.99 a month, a few cents under the yearly total divided by twelve. Solo is one user, Team carries unlimited users, and Office includes three with additional users at $9.99 each a month. Business texting carries a carrier cost on top of any plan: a one-time $19.50 registration fee and a $1.50 monthly compliance fee, which the FAQ says go to The Campaign Registry and the carriers and are due only once you activate texting; approval can take up to 10 business days. The plan set we recorded in August — Start-Up, Unlimited at $24.99 and Office-Max at $69.99 — is no longer offered. Support is US-based, there is a 30-day money-back guarantee, and every plan includes free professional recordings. The FAQ answer we flagged on 2026-09-09, which offered 3.9¢ per minute above the plan's minutes and named Office-Max, is no longer on the page.
